title: Principal curvature lines for tooth-level and smooth-transition boundaries
description:
Our current boundary detection is first-order (per-edge dihedral). This catches sharp creases (zygomatic lateral edges, tooth gaps at steep angles) but misses two important cases the user flagged:

1. Individual teeth: the gaps between adjacent molars are not always 30°+ creases — sometimes a smooth valley with moderate curvature separates them. Teeth boundaries are where the shape tensor's principal curvatures max/min transition, not where dihedrals spike.
2. Smooth anatomical transitions: the cheekbone (zygomatic process) rises from the cranium gradually — a curvature gradient, not a crease. Our feature-edge detection sees no ridge there so both regions merge.

Implement principal curvature line extraction following Ohtake, Belyaev & Seidel 2004 ('Ridge-Valley Lines on Meshes via Implicit Surface Fitting'):

1. Per-vertex shape tensor via local quadric fitting over 1-ring or 2-ring neighborhood.
2. Extract principal curvatures κ₁ ≥ κ₂ and their eigenvectors t₁, t₂.
3. Compute directional derivatives of κ₁ along t₁ (ridge test) and κ₂ along t₂ (valley test).
4. Trace zero-crossings of these derivatives as ridge/valley line segments.
5. Rasterize traced lines onto mesh edges: edges crossed by a ridge/valley line become 'feature edges' and join the dihedral-based feature set already driving the region-growing pass.

Implementation size: ~200 LOC. Shape tensor construction is the bulk; the rest is small.

References:
- Ohtake, Belyaev, Seidel 2004, 'Ridge-Valley Lines on Meshes via Implicit Surface Fitting'
- Kalogerakis et al. for a simpler per-vertex curvature estimator if Ohtake's tensor fitting is too heavy.

Originated from PATCH-1+2 follow-up user observation: 'still not seeing individual teeth, maybe do some research on the internet for how we could find those minimum and maximum curvature lines'.
definition-of-done: Per-vertex principal curvatures + ridge/valley line detection ship. Integrated into the feature-edge set in SemanticPatchDecomposer. Verified on skull: individual molars are distinct patches; cheekbone/cranium has a visible patch boundary along the zygomatic transition.
testing-plan: (1) On the skull, confirm at least 6 distinct tooth patches emerge (premolars + molars visible in the Bottom view). (2) On the skull, confirm the zygomatic process has a patch boundary separating it from the temporal bone — no more smooth merging.
